proof_n108.pdf argues: for each direction the verifier certifies that every closed square of side B at that direction with its centre in [w(a_r), L - w(a_r)]^2 captures mass at least one, w(t) = (1 + 2t - t^2)/(2(1 + t^2)) and a_r = max(0, rD - D/2); with z0 = D/2, u = 2B w(z0) = 319998768697057/320000086112500 and h = 707107/10^6 > 1/sqrt 2, the claimed side is S = 2h + (L - 2h)/u; a packing of 108 unit squares in [0, S]^2, scaled by u and translated by h(1 - u), lies in [0, L]^2 with each square's centre clear of every wall by at least its axis half-width, so each contains a core at its nearest grid direction inside the verified domain, and 108 cores with disjoint interiors would capture at least 108, more than the total mass. check_lower.py (Fraction arithmetic, standard library) is said to rebuild the measure, check the receipts' input and source hashes and one verified record per direction, integrate all eight images of every rectangle at the axis direction independently (minimum capture 1.007478833692, 0.997404045355 with every mass reduced by 1%) and check the enlargement; lower_checks.txt is its output. #1018 says the full replay has not been repeated independently, that the bound is not claimed to be close to optimal, asks for credit to Joost de Winter, Delft University of Technology, after Hiroaki Hosono, and says the rescaling, computation and proof were produced with GPT-6.2 Astra (OpenAI) and the repository files and checks with Claude (Anthropic), both under his direction. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
